en: his = belongs to a man or boy. her = belongs to a woman or girl.
The owner decides, not the thing: his mother, her father.
its = of a thing or animal, no apostrophe. it's = it is.
their = of several people or things.
es: his = de un hombre o niño. her = de una mujer o niña.
Importa quién es el dueño, no lo que se posee: his mother (la mamá de él), her father (el papá de ella).

en: Most verbs add -ed for the past: walked, opened.
Many common verbs change: go → went, see → saw, take → took.
The past form is the same for all persons: I went, she went.
Stories are told in the past, so the most common verbs are worth learning first.
es: La mayoría de los verbos agrega -ed en pasado: walked, opened.
Muchos verbos comunes cambian: go → went, see → saw, take → took.
El pasado es igual para todas las personas: I went, she went.
Los cuentos se narran en pasado, así que conviene aprender primero los verbos más comunes.

en: English sentences need a subject, even when Spanish drops it: She is tired.

En pasado (había): there was, there were: There was a door.

title.es: El orden de adjetivo y sustantivo

en: The adjective goes before the noun: a red door, an old man.
Adjectives never take -s: red doors, old men.
Noun + noun: the main thing goes last: a kitchen door is a door.
The first noun is usually singular: a shoe shop, a ten-year-old boy.
es: El adjetivo va antes del sustantivo: a red door, an old man.
Los adjetivos nunca llevan -s: red doors, old men.
Sustantivo + sustantivo: lo principal va al final: a kitchen door es una puerta.
El primer sustantivo suele ir en singular: a shoe shop, a ten-year-old boy.

en: Standard English uses one negative word per idea: I don't see anybody.

Or use a no- word alone: I said nothing. Nobody came.

O usa solo la palabra con no-: I said nothing. Nobody came.
En español sí se dice «No vi a nadie»; en inglés no.

en: Present perfect = have/has + past participle: I have seen it. Use it when the result matters now or the time is not finished.
Past simple = a finished time: I saw it yesterday. With yesterday, last week, in 2019 or ago, use the past simple.
With for and since, use the present perfect: I have lived here for ten years.
Ever, never, already, yet and just usually go with the present perfect.
es: Present perfect = have/has + participio: I have seen it (lo he visto). Se usa cuando importa el resultado ahora o el tiempo no ha terminado.
Past simple = un tiempo terminado: I saw it yesterday (lo vi ayer). Con yesterday, last week, in 2019 o ago se usa el past simple.
Con for y since se usa el present perfect: I have lived here for ten years (vivo aquí desde hace diez años).
Ever, never, already, yet y just suelen ir con el present perfect.

en: Age uses be: I am 20. You can add years old: I am twenty years old.
Feelings and states use be + adjective: I am hungry, thirsty, cold, hot, afraid.
Ask the age with How old: How old are you?
Careful: I am cold means you feel cold; I have a cold means you are ill.
es: La edad usa be: I am 20 (tengo 20 años). Puedes agregar years old: I am twenty years old.
Los estados usan be + adjetivo: I am hungry (tengo hambre), thirsty (sed), cold (frío), hot (calor), afraid (miedo).
La edad se pregunta con How old: How old are you? (¿cuántos años tienes?)
Ojo: I am cold es «tienes frío»; I have a cold es «estás resfriado».
